legacy_cells.C: Jorge M. Mendes; Aziz Barbar; Marwa Refaie
legacy_cells.I: 030_2025_Synthetic data generation a privacy-preserving approach to accelerate rare disease research.pdf
legacy_cells.FM: Synthesizes synthetic-data approaches and use cases for rare-disease research and proposes best practices addressing validation, ethical, regulatory, and quality considerations.
legacy_cells.FO: Discussed limitations of synthetic datasets include data quality, bias, validation, computational demands, incomplete realism, and privacy/security risks such as re-identification or model inversion.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify scarce patient data, strict privacy restrictions, and the need for diverse datasets as barriers to rare-disease research.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper is a perspective discussing synthetic-data approaches and cited examples; it does not report a newly implemented healthcare state representation, temporal transition, action-conditioned model, or world-model evaluation. Synthetic-data generation and cited static-task results do not demonstrate a healthcare world model.
legacy_cells.FT: Evaluate synthetic-data fidelity and downstream utility separately; validate against real-world data and involve domain experts rather than treating realism or privacy preservation alone as clinical utility.
legacy_cells.FX: Read title/byline/abstract and Introduction (PDF p. 1); all body sections including synthetic-data concepts, use cases, case studies, regulatory/ethical discussion, and current limitations (PDF pp. 2–5); Future perspectives, Conclusion, author statements (PDF p. 6); and all references (PDF pp. 7–8). No tables were present in the extracted text. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The paper is explicitly a perspective article and discusses synthetic-data methods and previously reported examples; it does not present a new model or original model-evaluation results.
